newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen says kidnappers won't destroy tourism sector.
newsitem.headline: Yemen says kidnappers won't destroy tourism sector.

text.p: Yemen's vice-president on Tuesday said tribesmen who had kidnapped dozens of foreigners in recent years would not damage the country's fledgling tourism industry.
"These mercenary attempts, that have tried and will try again to hurt Yemen's reputation and sabotage its image worldwide, will fail in achieving their goals," said Abd-Rabbu Mansour Hadi.

"The government security apparatus will take care of tourists and their programmes in Yemen and make all facilities available to them," he told the opening session of a three-day regional tourism conference in Sanaa.
Last week seven German tourists were freed after being held hostage by Yemeni tribesmen for nine days.

Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil companies have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips. All have been freed unharmed.
According to official figures released on Tuesday, some 75,000 tourists visited Yemen in 1996, up 20 percent from 1995. Tourism revenue rose to $75-80 million from about $30 million in previous year.
The private sector is currently executing tourism projects worth 6.1 billion rials ($48 million), the figures showed.
